newsitem.title: USA: Judge weighs up to 46-month sentence in muni case.
newsitem.headline: Judge weighs up to 46-month sentence in muni case.

text.p: U.S. District Judge William Young said Wednesday he is considering sentencing former municipal bond adviser Mark Ferber to between 37 months and 46 months for his conviction earlier this year on fraud and corruption charges.
Young also said during the first day of a sentencing hearing he believes Ferber "perjured himself" during his testimony in the trial.

A federal jury convicted Ferber in August of 58 of 61 counts of fraud and corruption in connection with a contract he maintained with Merrill Lynch & Co Inc to advise government clients on the municipal bond market.
Ferber argued that his tie to Merrill was a legitimate business arrangement. But Judge Young rejected the defense.

"His characterizations of his relationship with Merrill Lynch was a falsehood and he knew that," Young said. He said the relationship was "nothing more, nothing less than a rather grandiose kickback scheme."

Young also ordered a new trial on two counts of "honest services fraud," explaining that the jury's conviction on the counts contradicted another finding by the jury that Ferber was not guilty of "fraudulent intent to obtain money or profit."

In addition to the prison sentence, Young said he is considering a fine of not less than $7,500 and not more than $75,000. He said he is considering a supervised release following the prison term of between two and three years.
